items.description: The branch diff (main...HEAD) for ri-01 carries far more than the ri-01 plan: all 19 sibling scaffold changes, roadmap.yaml, checkpoint.json, the roadmap proposal, TRUST_POSTURE.md and openspec/supervise/supervisor-record.json. proposal.md's Non-Goals state 'No edits to roadmap.yaml or to sibling changes' artifacts', yet the PR that will be opened from this branch introduces them all. Either the roadmap bootstrap should land on main first (or in its own PR) or the proposal's scope statement must be corrected so reviewers know what they are approving.

reviews/consensus-plan.json records quorum_requested=1 and quorum_received=1 but quorum_met=false, and its summary has advisory_count=0 while three advisory (non-blocking) findings are listed. It also disagrees with reviews/review-manifest.json, which records zero successful dispatches (codex auth_required), quorum_received=0, vendors=[] and change_id=null, while consensus claims a successful claude_code reviewer with elapsed_seconds=0.0. The two review-record files describe different runs; downstream gating that reads either file gets contradictory answers about whether review happened.

loop-state.json (final gate note) and session-log.md both cite a TRUST_POSTURE.md section 'Review quorum in cloud containers (temporary)' at commit 479dcd9 as the authority for single-vendor review, but the TRUST_POSTURE.md in this diff contains no such section and no review-quorum policy at all. The recorded authorization points at content that is not in the committed contract.

design.md D3 states that when a roadmap capability is split, every resulting change-id inherits the capability's full Serves list. 'Ownership-routed escalation and attention budgets' serves P1, P3, P8, P10 and was split into owner-routed-escalation and attention-budgets-digests, but the P10 row lists only team-work-queue, queue-dispatch-owner-acceptance and owner-routed-escalation; attention-budgets-digests is missing from P10 while present in P1, P3 and P8. The mapping violates its own stated rule.

Requirement 'Solo and team mode vocabulary' says solo mode MUST be defined as the resolver yielding exactly one distinct human principal (including when owners.yaml is absent) and team mode as two or more, but no scenario checks any of that definitional content; the scenarios only check the bold terms, the exact guarantee sentence, the token 'ownership-map' and the phrase 'passive output'. The core definition the whole roadmap branches on is unguarded. If it is intentionally a review check, say so as the per-skill requirement does.

openspec/roadmaps/multiplayer-collaboration/checkpoint.json is stale relative to loop-state.json: its only dispatch attempt still reads outcome 'parked' on proposal_approval with a resume hint (updated_at 2026-10-05T07:06), while loop-state records that gate approved at 07:12 the same day and three later phases through 2026-10-09. A supervisor reading the checkpoint would re-issue a gate-answer that has already been given.

loop-state.json shows PLAN_REVIEW exiting with outcome 'max_iter' (and total_iterations=8, max_phase_iterations=3) yet findings_trend is empty and blocking_findings is empty. A phase that exhausted its iteration budget should have left a per-iteration findings trail; the empty trend makes the max_iter escalation unexplainable from the state file alone.

All 19 plan-roadmap scaffold specs use the placeholder pattern 'WHEN <change-id> is implemented THEN <acceptance outcome>', so every SHALL technically has a WHEN/THEN but none is a testable scenario, and requirement headings are truncated with '...' (e.g. 'Requirement: A roadmap item depending on a contract becomes a ready queue entry when its...'). The generator also lower-cases the first letter of each outcome, producing 'The system SHALL ensure that pRs created by ...' in reviewer-shaped-prs. Acceptable as flagged SCAFFOLD placeholders, but they must not be mistaken for reviewed specs, and the casing bug belongs in plan-roadmap.

TRUST_POSTURE.md sets replan_required to auto while its own summary table says 'merge and all failure/escalation gates block'. replan_required fires when a roadmap item's plan has failed and must be redone, which is a failure path; with proposal_approval also auto, a re-plan is produced and accepted with no human looking at it. The header comment attributes this to an operator decision, so this is recorded rather than contested.

TRUST_POSTURE.md says the approval gate service is 'roadmap item ri-05', but in the roadmap committed alongside it ri-05 is the simulation harness. The reference is to a different roadmap's item numbering and should name that roadmap (or the change-id) to avoid misdirecting readers.

openspec/supervise/supervisor-record.json has written_at 2026-10-05T06:59:55.764282Z, which precedes the decided_at 06:59:55.799843 of the decision it records. The write timestamp is being captured before the decision timestamp, so ordering by written_at misrepresents causality.

checkpoint.json commits a dispatch launch_token and lease owner_nonce to git. If these values are ever used to authenticate a marker or lease claim (rather than merely to disambiguate), committing them defeats that purpose; if they are not secrets, a comment or schema note should say so.

Re-verification of ledger item 4: FIXED in the artifacts. docs/guides/multiplayer-collaboration.md P10 Planned line and design.md D3 table P10 row now both include `attention-budgets-digests`, so the split-capability inheritance rule is applied consistently. However .review-ledger/ledger.json still records item 4 with status "open" and last_seen_round 1; the ledger was not updated when the IMPLEMENT phase applied the carry-forward fix (session-log 'Carry-forward fixes in design.md'). Mark item 4 resolved so the review record matches the tree.

Re-verification of ledger item 5: PARTIALLY addressed. design.md D5 now states that the `## Modes` solo/team definition has no test scenario and is checked in review, but the spec requirement 'Solo and team mode vocabulary' (the normative text) still asserts the definition with MUST and provides no scenario for it, nor the 'checked in review' clause that the per-skill requirement carries. Add one sentence to the requirement ('Whether the definition is correct is checked in review; the guard test checks only the terms and the guarantee sentence') so spec and design agree.

Re-verification of ledger items 1, 2 and 3: all STILL OPEN and unchanged in this round. (1) The branch still carries the whole roadmap bootstrap (19 scaffolds, roadmap.yaml, checkpoint.json, roadmap proposal, TRUST_POSTURE.md, supervisor-record.json) while proposal.md Non-Goals says no edits to roadmap.yaml or sibling artifacts. (2) reviews/consensus-plan.json (quorum_received=1, quorum_met=false, advisory_count=0 with three advisory findings, claude_code success) still contradicts reviews/review-manifest.json (quorum_received=0, vendors=[], change_id=null, codex auth_required). (3) TRUST_POSTURE.md still contains no 'Review quorum in cloud containers (temporary)' section, yet loop-state.json gate note and session-log.md cite it at 479dcd9 as the authority for single-vendor review. Items 1 and 3 require an operator decision (land the bootstrap separately or amend the proposal scope; commit the quorum policy section or re-point the citation); item 2 is a stale-file cleanup.

Re-verification of ledger items 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12: all STILL OPEN and unchanged. checkpoint.json still shows ri-01 parked on proposal_approval (6); loop-state.json findings_trend is still empty despite max_iter and total_iterations now 11 (7); scaffold specs unchanged including the 'pRs created by' casing bug (8); replan_required still auto (9, recorded operator decision); TRUST_POSTURE.md still says 'roadmap item ri-05' for the approval gate service (10); supervisor-record.json written_at still precedes decided_at (11); launch_token/owner_nonce still committed without a non-secret note (12). Items 10 and 11 are one-line fixes.

session-log.md 'Plan Iteration 1' Context paragraph is corrupted by sanitization: the text reads '...restoring the lost prior attempt[REDACTED:high-entropy]Resume with single reviewer acceptable". This matches the committed cloud policy...' and is followed by an orphaned '2. **Review diff base**' list item with no item 1. The redaction swallowed the sentence boundary and the start of the numbered decision list, so the record of the user's acceptance of single-vendor review (which the later 'Plan Review' entry cites as 'the user-accepted decision above') is only partially present in the committed log. Reconstruct the paragraph from the handoff/gate-decision e49a71df and fix the sanitizer's token boundary handling as a toolkit follow-up.

loop-state.json carries stale phase metadata: current_phase is IMPL_REVIEW (after IMPLEMENT and IMPL_ITERATE completed on 2026-10-09) but previous_phase is still 'PLAN_REVIEW' and escalation_reason still reads "PLAN_REVIEW transitioned to ESCALATE via outcome 'max_iter'" although that escalation was resolved at 08:03 and PLAN_REVIEW later converged. phase_archetype is 'implementer' for a review phase. A rehydrating session reading these fields would misread the loop as freshly escalated out of plan review.

proposal.md 'What Changes' describes each principle as having 'an *Implemented by* line', while design.md D3, the spec requirement 'Principles are stated with implementers', the guard test and the guide all use two lines, `**Existing:**` and `**Planned:**`. The proposal is the artifact reviewers approve; align its wording with the spec so the approved scope names the mechanism actually built.

Per-skill table content check (design D5 says cell accuracy is a review check): the Solo mode cell for `implement-feature` attributes commit trailers to `attribution-trailers`, but that change stamps On-Behalf-Of / Correlation-Id trailers on all skill-authored commits and PR bodies. `autopilot` and `cleanup-feature` also author commits and PRs, yet their Solo mode cells list only the PR ledger section and their Delivered by cells omit `attribution-trailers`. Either add the trailer output (and change-id) to those rows or state that the trailer behavior is listed once under implement-feature.

TRUST_POSTURE.md summary table says pr_creation 'Fails closed if the notification is undelivered', but the Dispositions section defines notify_with_timeout solely in terms of timeout_seconds expiry and default_action; no undelivered-notification behavior is described, and with default_action: proceed a reader cannot tell whether an undelivered notification parks the loop or proceeds after an hour. Document the undelivered path in the Dispositions table (or drop the claim) so the active contract describes the behavior the gate service actually implements.
